subject: Renewal: Multi-year structure & ramp options (NovaCorp)
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novacorp.com>, NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal coming up — exploring 2/3 yr options + ramping

Hi Aditya,

Our renewal for the 2026 subscription is coming up in July. Weve been very happy with the latency gains on inference and want to lock in capacity while keeping flexibility for a fast-growing 2028 product line.

High level asks:
- Interested in a multi-year commitment (2 or 3 years) with a graduated ramp rather than a flat annual commit.
- Need clear true-up mechanics and a co-terming option that aligns to our fiscal year (Oct 1).
- Wed like an opt-out window for auto-renew (60 days before term) and a limit on price increases.

Can you share the options you typically propose for customers with bursty growth? Also please cc legal/procurement guidance if you need it.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
VP Engineering, NovaCorp


From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novacorp.com>, NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — exploring 2/3 yr options + ramping

Elena — thanks for the clear asks, happy to put forward a couple of anchored options. I attached a short proposal with pricing bands and ramp schedules. Quick summary below: 

Option A — 2yr Graduated Commit (recommended):
- Year 1: 60% of projected peak; Year 2: 100% (step-up in Q3 of Year 1).
- True-ups quarterly; overage billing monthly at committed unit rates.
- Co-term to Oct 1 with prorated Year 1 credits for the partial period.
- Auto-renew enabled by default with 60-day opt-out window; price increase cap 5% annual.

Option B — 3yr Anchored + Burst Pool:
- Year 1: 50%; Year 2: 80%; Year 3: 120% (built-in growth headroom).
- Includes a shared burst pool with guaranteed eviction SLAs.
- Can include a fixed-rate floor to protect both sides.

Operational notes:
- We recommend quarterly true-ups to avoid large end-of-term bills.
- Dedicated ramp credits can be frontloaded to help your Q4 launch.
- Ill loop in Camila (sales ops) and Karthik (legal) for contract mechanics.

Attached: Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (pricing + ramp schedules) and a draft SOW outline.

Next step: Would you like a short call this week to walk through tradeoffs?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal coming up — exploring 2/3 yr options + ramping

Camila / Karthik — forwarding Elenas note and my initial two options. Can you please: 
1) Camila — confirm how we should price the burst pool vs committed units and whether we can offer a small onboarding credit (one-off) to smooth Year 1. Also advise on billing cadence if they co-term to Oct 1.
2) Karthik — review the auto-renew + price-cap language and the suggested 60-day opt-out. Any concerns with compliance or standard redlines?

Id like a consolidated proposal by EOD Fri so I can present a final to NovaCorp next week. Attaching the v1 proposal.

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachments: Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal coming up — exploring 2/3 yr options + ramping

Thanks Aditya — quick ops/legal points after a skim: 

Pricing & billing:
- Burst pool: charge at 30% premium to committed unit rate, with a monthly cap equal to 25% of committed spend (keeps tail risk manageable).
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time credit equal to 5% of Year 1 committed ARR, applied on first invoice.
- Co-term: if they pick Oct 1 co-term, we will prorate the interim period and apply remaining credits to the first co-term year.

Contract language (Karthik feel free to redline):
- Auto-renew: acceptable with a 60-day explicit opt-out notice; we should add an explicit annual price change notice clause and a maximum price increase of 5% unless mutually agreed.
- True-up: quarterly true-up recommended; include a 90-day dispute window for measured usage.
- Cancellation: allow a one-time early termination for material breach only; otherwise standard termination for convenience not allowed on committed pricing.

I attached a doc with suggested redlines (redlines_legal_comments.docx). If Karthik signs off Ill update the proposal with the credit and burst premium.

Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novacorp.com>, NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — exploring 2/3 yr options + ramping

Aditya / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and thoughtful options. We reviewed Option A vs B internally. A few clarifications before we proceed to procurement: 

- The 60-day opt-out works for us as written but request that the notice window can be sent to procurement@novacorp.com and a delegated approver to avoid missing it.
- We prefer quarterly true-ups but ask that the first true-up be delayed until the end of Q1 post-co-term to give us time to instrument telemetry for the new product.
- Please incorporate the 5% onboarding credit and the burst pool premium into a revised proposal.

If you can share updated SOW (with the co-term mechanics and the revised billing schedule) we can route to procurement. Once legal confirms the minor redlines well sign.

Best,
Elena Morales
VP Engineering, NovaCorp
